event.summary: Old-terminal cleanup may leave a running agent beside Restart; explicitly accepted
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f96dd4363d97dc7e07dea5b8947c96be6bf912e8.
TLDR: An update can mark an old terminal ended even when its agent could not be stopped; Restart can then run a second agent in the same folder. Concurrent agents could damage user work.
Details: The changed old-terminal paragraph at SPEC.md:2998–3009 retains failure-tolerant startup. SPEC_impl.md:2786–2823 describes the bounded startup cleanup and says conversion commits even when cleanup runs out of time. At crates/farhelm-supervisor/src/service/core/old_terminals.rs:176–278, failed identification, connection or termination returns no subtree roots or logs a surviving server, without failing startup. Its module contract at lines 67–84 explicitly permits this. This is source and contract analysis, not observed execution.
Suggested bucket: highest (could lose user-owned work if agents concurrently edit it). Confidence: confirmed for the accepted duplicate-agent route; actual file damage is conditional on the agents' activity. Could-be-highest: yes.
proposed_drop: Explicit acceptance retained by this documentation patch, not a new relaxation. Exact SPEC.md:3006–3009 text: ‘A failure to end the server or to stop what ran there is logged and never stops the supervisor from starting; those sessions are treated as ended all the same, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running. Restart, Clone and Replace start such a session in a new, empty terminal.’ SPEC_impl.md:2818–2821 likewise says: ‘A failure anywhere is logged and never fatal (the maintainer chose to start anyway and treat old sessions as ended, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running)’. The parent must obtain the required independent drop check before dropping this potentially highest finding.
possible_cover: the cited SPEC.md and SPEC_impl.md explicit acceptance only; no queue or other coverage searched. Caveat: assigned patch changes wording and removes retired behavior descriptions; it does not introduce the implementation route.

event.summary: Removing the old launch-excerpt contamination caveat is supported
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f96dd4363d97dc7e07dea5b8947c96be6bf912e8.
TLDR: Considered whether a failed Restart could quote the previous run’s terminal output after this patch removed the old-terminal caveat. Source refutes that path for terminal hosts.
Details: SPEC.md:2892–2897 removes the exception for a tmux terminal retaining an earlier run’s screen. Restart still preserves history, but crates/farhelm-supervisor/src/service/launch_artifacts.rs:59–75 quotes only host.screen_tail after owned-dead evidence. hosts/terminal.rs:2229–2239 and farhelm-terminal-emulator/src/emulator.rs:265–275 show that this reads the visible screen rather than history. farhelm-terminal-emulator/src/snapshot/mod.rs:541–569 delegates Restart’s seed to encode_history, whose implementation in snapshot/v1/mod.rs:242–268 paints primary history above a blank screen, not the prior visible frame. SPEC_impl.md:2657–2668 gives the same contract, including waiting for drained output. This is source analysis only.
Suggested bucket: other if it existed (misleading launch diagnosis). Confidence: confirmed refutation of the considered route. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route; quoting a prior error alone would misdiagnose a failed launch.
proposed_drop: Refuted by the visible-screen-only quote and history-only Restart seed at the cited source locations. possible_cover: none. Caveat: this does not claim terminal-host recovery or arbitrary emulator behavior was independently reviewed; the assigned change only removes the retired tmux exception.
